chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام heard, on the Day of ʿArafah, a beggar asking the people, so he said to him:
"Woe to you! Are you asking anyone other than Allah on this day? Indeed, it is hoped for what is in the wombs of pregnant women on this day that it may be happy."

key_terms.اللَّهِ: Allah, the one from whom one should seek on this day
key_terms.النَّاسَ: the people being asked by the beggar
key_terms.سَائِلًا: a beggar or one asking for help
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: the Day of ʿArafah, a greatly blessed day in hajj

ai.seo_question: Why should a believer ask Allah alone on the Day of ʿArafah?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the immense spiritual virtue of the Day of ʿArafah and directs a person to turn to Allah alone in need and hope. It portrays the day as one of vast divine mercy, such that happiness is hoped even for those still in the wombs of pregnant women.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2182 - Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn (as) heard a beggar asking people on the Day of Arafah.

He said to him: "Woe to you! Are you asking anyone other than Allah (swt) on this day? Indeed, it is hoped that even what is in the wombs of pregnant women will be destined for happiness on this day."
